facts.raw_span: 2-year history of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
occasional slight pain extending from her left upper arm to the left side of her chest
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
She denied fever, weight loss, or fatigue
Multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders on her left axilla, medial upper arm, and lateral thoracic region
No extracutaneous involvement was observed
Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Positive for: CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Negative for: podoplanin (D2-40), human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)
Image A Description: Multiple nonscaly, erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders on the patient's left axilla, medial upper arm, and lateral thoracic region
Image B Description: Irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels dissecting through collagen bundles within the superficial to mid dermis
Image D Description: Endothelial cells positive for cluster of differentiation (CD) 31

concepts.why: The presence of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34 are consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma.
The clinical presentation of multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders is consistent with a hemangioma.

The presence of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34, along with the absence of significant cytologic atypia, are consistent with an angiosarcoma.
The clinical presentation of multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders is consistent with a lymphangioma.
The presence of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels is consistent with a vascular malformation.

The presence of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34, along with the absence of significant cytologic atypia, are consistent with a malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
The clinical presentation of multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders is consistent with a dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.

The presence of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34, along with the absence of significant cytologic atypia, are consistent with a leiomyosarcoma.

The patient's histopathological examination and immunohistochemistry results, including negativity for podoplanin (D2-40) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8), are consistent with Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
